$comment: Compatibility manifest for the controlled downgrade (see the controlled-downgrade conception, lot A).
The CLI READS this file and never infers compatibility from a version number, so a release that is
not described here can only ever be told to restore from a backup -- which is the safe direction.
TWO targets are offered, both measured: 1.6.15 (the release immediately preceding 1.7, published
2026-09-21) and 1.6.14. A pair is looked up on (from, to, engine), so `bwcli plugin backup downgrade
1.6.15` and `... 1.6.14` each pick their own row. 1.6.15 is the shorter path -- two revisions instead
of six -- and the one to prefer; see the notes on the 1.6.14 rows for what the extra four cost.
'from' is matched against /usr/share/bunkerweb/VERSION verbatim. BUMP IT WITH src/VERSION: a stale
'from' makes every pair unmatched and pins the product to restore_only. tests/unit/backup/
test_downgrade_manifest.py fails when the two disagree, so the bump cannot be forgotten silently.
MEASURED, per engine, by an executed upgrade+downgrade: `mode`, `data_loss`, every `fingerprint`

field, and each `restore_only` reason. The main run carries sentinel data; the structural blocker in  the restore_only reasons was measured by re-running the same probe with NO sentinel rows, so that the
data-dependent blocker is not reached first. Each reason names the artefact it was read from.
built from `git show v<target>:src/common/db/model.py`, seeded, upgraded to the 1.7 head, seeded again
with 1.7-only rows and then downgraded back. 1.6.14: .cache/results-2026-09-06-wave13/report-DG-AD.md
and dgad-probe-*.json. 1.6.15: .cache/wave21-2026-09-21/report-DG-1615.md and dg1615-probe-*.json.
`generated_at` is the date of the most recent measurement in this file, which is what the staleness
guard in tests/unit/backup/test_downgrade_manifest.py compares against the head's Create Date. It is NOT
a claim that every row was re-taken on that date: the 1.6.14 fingerprints are wave 13's (2026-09-06),
re-confirmed on the post-1.6.16~rc1 chain for the landing revision and version on SQLITE ONLY (dg1615-drafts-1614.json); the other three engines' 1.6.14 fingerprints were NOT re-run this wave.
The 1.6.15 rows were measured on all four engines on 2026-09-21, as were both blockers behind the mariadb/mysql restore_only verdicts.
DERIVED, not measured: the `artifacts` map. It comes from reading the tree (src/common/helpers/data.sh
is byte-identical between v1.6.14, v1.6.15 and 1.7, so the /data layout cannot have moved) and from what
each job regenerates, not from a downgrade run. Treat those values as a documented expectation.

fingerprint.method: 1.6.14 create_all -> stamp -> sentinel rows -> alembic upgrade head -> 1.7-only sentinel rows -> alembic downgrade to 1.6.14 (six revisions run since the 1.6.15/1.6.16~rc1 chain landed: the 1.7.0~beta head, 1.6.16~rc1, 1.6.15, 1.6.15~rc3, 1.6.15~rc2, 1.6.15~rc1)
fingerprint.baseline_row_delta_explained: +1: bw_ui_user_preferences is renamed back into bw_ui_user_columns_preferences rather than dropped
fingerprint.target_model_select_failures_detail: bw_ui_user_columns_preferences raised JSONDecodeError. An artifact of the probe's own sentinel, which wrote a non-JSON string into bw_ui_user_preferences.value before the downgrade renamed the table; real 1.7 preference values are JSON documents. The renamed-back rows still reach 1.6.14 as the wrong KIND of preference -- see the note below.

notes: Every table and column the 1.6.14 model declares is present after the downgrade, with no extras.

Non-column user preferences (theme_mode, whats_new, onboarding, walkthrough) reappear in 1.6.14 as bogus per-table column layouts: the downgrade renames bw_ui_user_preferences to bw_ui_user_columns_preferences wholesale instead of filtering the column-layout keys. Expected to be cosmetic rather than a crash, because every writer in src/ui/app/routes/ stores a JSON document -- but that is read off the callers, NOT measured: the probe's own sentinel was not JSON and did raise JSONDecodeError through the 1.6.14 model.

MEASURED 2026-09-21 on SQLite (dg1615-drafts-1614.json), and NOT reflected in `mode`. Engine-independent by construction: the refusal is a Python RuntimeError raised inside the migration, before any DDL is emitted, and the four engines' 1.6.15~rc3 revisions are byte-identical Python. It is since the 1.6.15/1.6.16~rc1 chain landed, this path runs 1.6.15~rc3's downgrade(), which REFUSES with "Cannot downgrade individual setting drafts while bw_global_values contains draft rows" when bw_global_values or bw_services_settings still holds is_draft = 1 -- dropping the flag would silently activate the retained value. The run then stops stamped at the 1.6.15~rc3 revision with bw_metadata.version = '1.6.15~rc3'; `bwcli plugin backup downgrade --execute` catches that and restores its own pre-downgrade backup, so nothing is lost, but the preflight said in_place_possible first and does NOT count draft rows. 1.7 cannot create or clear them (its model declares is_draft on bw_services and bw_custom_configs only), so this is reachable exactly on an installation that made individual setting drafts under 1.6.15~rc3 or later and then upgraded. The 1.6.15 target stops above that revision and is unaffected -- prefer it.

notes: Two enum TYPES the 1.7 upgrade creates are not dropped by the downgrade (instance_tls_mode_enum, resource_kinds_enum), and the values added to api_resource_enum and settings_types_enum cannot be removed at all -- PostgreSQL has no ALTER TYPE ... DROP VALUE. Measured harmless: 1.6.14 never references them, the one SELECT failure the probe recorded is its own non-JSON sentinel (see target_model_select_failures_detail) and not these types, and a later re-upgrade is idempotent (CREATE TYPE ... EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object, ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS).
Those leftover values are also what SAVES PostgreSQL where MariaDB/MySQL fail: bw_ui_users.method keeps 'api' as a legal label instead of having the enum narrowed under it.

releases.reason: The 1.7 head's downgrade() does not run to completion on MariaDB. Two independent blockers. (1) Data-dependent, MEASURED here (dgad-probe-mariadb.json): ALTER TABLE bw_ui_users MODIFY method ENUM('ui','scheduler','autoconf','manual','wizard') fails with error 1265 'Data truncated for column method' on any row holding 'api', a value 1.7 added and the API sets. (2) Structural and data-independent, MEASURED 2026-09-21 on this engine (.cache/wave21-2026-09-21/proofs/dg1615-probe-empty-mariadb.json -- the same probe re-run with no sentinel rows, so (1) is not reached; wave 13 could only take it from lane LR-v's report-LR.md 6.2): DROP INDEX ix_bw_resource_group_usages_plugin_id fails with error 1553, 'needed in a foreign key constraint', on an index drop_table makes redundant. That run targets 1.6.15, and it covers this pair too: the abort is inside the 1.7 head's own downgrade(), which both targets execute in full. Both are byte-identical in the previous 1.7 beta heads and are never executed by product code. Worse than a plain refusal: the failure is partial. The first statement of downgrade() commits the bw_metadata version bump under MariaDB's non-transactional DDL, so a failed attempt leaves bw_metadata.version at 1.6.16~rc1 while alembic_version still names the 1.7 head and the schema is a hybrid -- a state the preflight refuses and the scheduler entrypoint cannot recover from. Restore from backup is the only path.

fingerprint.method: same probe as sqlite/postgresql; the downgrade aborted mid-way

releases.reason: The 1.7 head's downgrade() does not run to completion on MySQL 8 either. Blocker (1) was MEASURED separately here on a real MySQL 8 (dgad-probe-mysql.json): ALTER TABLE bw_ui_users MODIFY method ENUM(...) fails with error 1265 on a row holding 'api'. Blocker (2), the error-1553 index drop, was INFERRED for MySQL in wave 13 and is MEASURED as of 2026-09-21 (.cache/wave21-2026-09-21/proofs/dg1615-probe-empty-mysql.json -- the same probe re-run on a real MySQL 8 with no sentinel rows, so (1) is not reached): DROP INDEX ix_bw_resource_group_usages_plugin_id fails with error 1553, 'needed in a foreign key constraint', exactly as on MariaDB. Both targets execute the same head downgrade(), so the measurement taken for the 1.6.15 pair covers this one. Either blocker alone is enough for restore_only. The version bump in bw_metadata has already committed when it aborts, so the database is left claiming 1.6.16~rc1 on a hybrid schema. Restore from backup is the only path.

data_loss_detail.$comment: Applies to every in_place_tested pair above. 'certain' = the rows are destroyed and cannot be recreated; 'conditional' = destroyed but regenerable, with a stated cost. The preflight counts the live rows and compares them against this map.

why.bw_bans: regenerable by the sync-bans job, which relearns from the instances' shared dicts and Redis; ban durations and tombstones are lost
why.bw_ui_user_preferences: renamed back into bw_ui_user_columns_preferences rather than dropped, so the rows survive; only their meaning is lost (every key becomes a per-table column layout)
why.bw_ui_user_webauthn_credentials: every registered passkey; a passkey-only user must fall back to password + TOTP
why.bw_certificates: every centrally stored certificate and private key
why.bw_metrics_requests: all request metrics and the threat map history
why.bw_resources: every attachable resource, and by foreign key the redirects, upstream pools, workflows and resource groups keyed on it

data_loss_detail.columns_why: Dropped by the downgrade on every engine, on the way to 1.6.14. The bw_instances credential and enrolment columns matter most: every enrolled instance has to be re-registered against the global API_TOKEN after a rollback. One entry is target-dependent: bw_ui_users.totp_last_counter is dropped by 1.6.15~rc2's downgrade, which the 1.6.15 target does not reach, so a rollback to 1.6.15 keeps it. This map is the union, so it never under-states a loss; it over-states that single column for the 1.6.15 pairs.

not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_metrics_baseline: observability, not configuration, and always non-empty -- counting it would pin every installation to restore_only forever
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_ui_user_preferences: every UI user has rows here (theme, dismissed notices, onboarding progress, what's-new stamps, column layouts), so counting it would pin every installation to restore_only. Not destroyed outright: the downgrade renames the table back to bw_ui_user_columns_preferences, so the rows survive and only their meaning is lost
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_resource_attachments: covered transitively: every row keys on bw_resources, which IS counted, so this table is empty whenever that one is
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_resource_group_entries: covered transitively: an entry keys on a group, and the operator-built groups ARE counted (bw_resource_groups WHERE plugin_id IS NULL). A seeded group cannot be given operator entries either -- update_resource_group refuses when method is not editable -- so what is left here is re-seeded by the next upgrade
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_resource_group_usages: a usage row is the index of which plugin consumes which group; it is rebuilt from the settings that reference the group, and those settings are 1.6.x rows the downgrade keeps. Not empty when a seeded group is in use, which is why it is not counted
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_upstream_servers: covered transitively: every row keys on bw_upstreams, which IS counted
